candidates.change_summary: Return a different 4-byte selector by changing ERC721TokenReceiver.onERC721Received.selector to a different constant
Removed the assignment `baseToken = _baseToken;` so baseToken retains its default value (address(0)) after initialize is called.
Changed the assignment to `baseToken = address(0);` so baseToken is always set to the zero address regardless of the _baseToken parameter.
Changed the assignment to `baseToken = _nft;` so baseToken is incorrectly set to the NFT address.
Replace the `nft` assignment with a constant zero address to ensure it always differs from the original input.
Assign `nft` to the `msg.sender` address instead of the provided `_nft` parameter.
Delete the `nft = _nft;` assignment so `nft` remains its default zero value.
Replace assignment `changeFee = _changeFee;` with `changeFee = 0;` so the stored fee differs from the argument.
Replace assignment `changeFee = _changeFee;` with `changeFee = _changeFee + 1;` causing stored fee to be one greater than the argument.
Replace assignment `changeFee = _changeFee;` with `changeFee = uint56(uint256(_changeFee) + 1e18);` drastically altering the stored fee.
Delete the assignment `changeFee = _changeFee;` so `changeFee` remains its default zero value.
Delete the fee-rate-too-high check, so an initialize call can set feeRate above 5000, changing the observable stored value.
Replace the feeRate assignment with a constant 0, so initialize always stores 0 regardless of the argument.
Replace the feeRate assignment with _feeRate + 1, incrementing the stored fee rate.

Move the feeRate assignment before the fee-rate-too-high check, so it is stored even when _feeRate > 5000 and the call reverts, but the observable behavior is that a successful call still stores the valid _feeRate.
